doc.title: Phil Mead interviewed by Monk Rowe, Clinton, New York, June 1, 2006

title: Improvising by ear and advice to young players
summary: He improvises by hearing, not chords; licks recur as with Teagarden; advice is to listen to good music.

story.theme_name: Teaching jazz: schools, students and advice to the young
story.community_name: What to think while improvising: wrong notes and being in the moment

blocks.x: That’s good. When you improvise on a particular song, are there things that are going through your head as far as note choices relating to chords or is it more of a hearing —

It’s almost exclusively hearing because I’m not trained in chords. And actually the guy I’m studying trombone with now, who is a fine classical, he’s tried to teach me the chord thing and I can’t do it. And it’s because it’s so much easier to do it the other way and I guess at age 69 it doesn’t make a whole lot of sense to learn a hard way to do something.

But the thing that I do notice about my improvising is that as I am now playing a lot more you begin to, there are just certain licks that you put into your brain that come out and that didn’t happen before, and I sort of agree with the people that say, I still think that’s improvising. Because you play it a little differently every time.
And if you listen to Teagarden, I mean if you listen to his breaks on “Royal Garden Blues,” you know half of the time they’re the same ones. But why not? They’re spectacular.

He plays them a little differently and it’s not like a symphonic trombonist who would play this measure and it would sound exactly the same every time. No. So I do notice that change now, which is I think good, not bad.

Well don’t let your teacher spoil you by making you do something that seems unnatural. You know some of the greatest players, Zoot Sims and those fellas, are not as it’s called schooled in that, but the ears are all-important.

You’ve got to listen all the time. When young players ask me, “What should I do,” just listen to good people all the time, and it doesn’t particularly matter. I even listen to some symphonic stuff. But just listen to good music all the time. And it’s certainly easy advice to follow.
